issue.standard_remedy: Consolidate tail suppliers into preferred suppliers
issue.summary: 114 of 153 suppliers share the last 20% of category spend

plan.diagnosis: The Rubber compounds category exhibits extreme fragmentation with an HHI of 458 (well below the 1,500 consolidation threshold) and 114 suppliers sharing only 20% ($1,984,427) of total category spend ($10,075,096). This tail fragmentation creates excessive transactional overhead, minimal volume leverage, and increases compliance risk across 153 total suppliers where the top supplier holds only 10.8% share.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct tail spend analysis to identify the 114 suppliers delivering $1,984,427 and map their SKUs, volumes, and business criticality; shortlist 3-5 preferred suppliers capable of absorbing tail volume

Launch competitive RFQ with shortlisted preferred suppliers (including Oakridge Pacific Metals Manufacturing Co. as anchor) targeting consolidation of $1,984,427 tail spend with 15-20% volume leverage discount
Negotiate master agreements with 2-3 winning suppliers incorporating tier-based pricing, consolidated payment terms (Net 60), and minimum volume commitments
Implement ERP changes across all systems to block tail suppliers and route demand to preferred suppliers via source lists and catalog restrictions
Execute supplier offboarding communication plan for 100+ tail suppliers, close open POs, and migrate spend over 90-day transition window

plan.expected_impact: Consolidating the $1,984,427 tail spend into 2-3 preferred suppliers is expected to yield $297,664 in annual savings (15% volume leverage) plus $150,000 in reduced transactional costs from eliminating 100+ supplier relationships.
kpis: Reduce supplier count from 153 to <50 within 6 months
Reduce tail spend share from 20% to <10% of category spend
Decrease PO count by 60% in Rubber compounds category
risks: Supply continuity risk if tail suppliers hold unique formulations or serve niche applications not covered by preferred suppliers
Preferred supplier capacity constraints absorbing $1.98M in additional volume
Resistance from decentralized plants with entrenched tail supplier relationships across SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, and NetSuite
Extended transition timelines if tail suppliers hold long-lead tooling or custom molds
Quality issues during supplier transitions requiring dual-sourcing overlap periods
erp_actions: SAP: Apply posting block in LFB1 (vendor-company) and purchasing block in LFM1 (vendor-purchasing org) for 100+ tail suppliers post-transition
Oracle EBS: Set supplier status to 'Inactive' in PO module and remove from approved supplier lists for Rubber compounds commodity code
Dynamics 365: Create source list entries mapping Rubber compounds item groups to 2-3 preferred suppliers with exclusive sourcing flags
NetSuite: Update vendor records with 'Do Not Use' status for tail suppliers and configure approval workflows to block requisitions
Coupa: Deactivate tail supplier catalogs, enable preferred supplier content, and configure guided buying to route 100% of Rubber compounds demand to contracted suppliers
All ERPs: Change payment terms to Net 60 for preferred suppliers to improve working capital; consolidate remittance to single AP contact per supplier
